title: Cross-Lab Eval Divergence x Single-Score Indices: Sensitivity Analysis of the AI Safety Index

original_idea.body:
# Cross-Lab Eval Divergence x Single-Score Indices: Sensitivity Analysis of the AI Safety Index

**Problem:** Different evaluators grade differently; composite indices collapse grades into one headline letter. Grade noise compounds into a falsely-precise ranking.

**Direction:** Reconstruct the published Index scoring (33 indicators, 6 domains, unweighted averaging) and run a sensitivity/bootstrap analysis; measure how often lab ranking flips.

**Why it matters:** Shows how much of a widely-cited governance signal is real vs aggregation noise. Pure re-analysis of a public report.

**Relevant context:** FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2025 (futureoflife.org); FR67 hint.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (more robust safety rankings improve incentives) but the catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Bootstrap/sensitivity re-analysis of a public scorecard; accessible to a beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single re-analysis with clear success criterion (ranking-flip frequency).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure public-report re-analysis; civil-society methodology improvement labs won't do.

novelty.reasoning: Index-sensitivity methods are standard; applying to this specific Index may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Sensitivity analysis is standard but its application to the FLI Index ranking robustness may be open.
